value.rationale: The volume product is a central affine invariant, and coordinate clipping of classical ℓp balls is a naturally motivated family linking polar volume growth and primal volume loss. Showing that truncation improves the product in every dimension exactly for 1<p<2, and that the improving depth has one strict global maximum, resolves the complete geometric optimization rather than a local numerical instance. The p=2 threshold is a structural qualitative phenomenon and the monotonic criterion is reusable for polar-section problems. No claim about general Mahler extremizers is made.
